title: Proof
$comment: AUTHORED object (§5.1): produced by an actor and validated against this schema. STUB. Tracks §5 of WISHMAIL_SPEC_v0_5.md field for field. Not yet registered under HCS-13: spec/pins.json registeredSchemas is null for this object (T-P9-4, T-P9-9). The specification leads, the schema follows, the tests are the court: where a constraint below is not expressible in JSON Schema, the named test is what holds it.

rule.description: What fired: a profile at its pin, or a WISHMail rule at this specification’s version.

inputs.description: Digest of the canonical input bytes; a structured locator that dereferences to them (form per §9 / §10); for inputs not on consensus, a snapshot of the bytes read (§9.1).

locator.description: Structured, never a string (§5.2). Its shape is the profile’s or the proof kind’s (§9, §10).

snapshot.description: The bytes a rule read from a source that is not on consensus (§2.2, §9.1). REQUIRED for a non-consensus profile: T-P6-2 rejects a manifest without one at `send`.

output.description: What the rule produced: {digest} or a value (§5.2).

meaning.description: The reasoner’s statement of what the output means; the canonical location; what its verification rests on; what it could not see.

uri.description: The canonical location: the topic the proof's manifest is published on (§5.2, D-163). A LOCATION and not a locator — it names a topic and no message, because a proof's hash covers its meaning and its manifest is published after the hash is fixed (§6.4). The manifest at a location is the message on that topic whose body recomputes to the proof's hash; the precise message locator lives in a reference, never here.

ledgerTag.description: Ledger tag (§5.1). The core defines exactly these two and refuses every other; an extension that claims another ledger widens this enum (§16.7).
ledgerTag.$comment: T-P9-11 — an envelope whose AAD names an undefined ledger tag is rejected at send and appraises unbound at replay.

uri.$comment: T-P6-7 — a proof whose location holds no message recomputing to its hash appraises no higher than unverified (§11.1, §11.5). Not an HRL: the HCS-1 HRL grammar names files, not topics on which messages are published.

endorsements.description: Endorsements — what the proof could not see (§2.2). Orthogonal to trust class.

hash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of {rule, inputs, output, meaning} with `hash` absent (§5.1).
